problem: Video-3DGS pipelines (Vid2Sim, GaussGym) built from casual touring videos have inaccurate, non-metric reconstruction, fragmented collision geometry and poor extrapolated-view rendering, so they cannot serve as reliable closed-loop benchmarks for open-world navigation. Classic RGB-D datasets (Matterport3D, HM3D) are indoor-only.
motivation: Reproducible closed-loop evaluation of urban/open-world navigation needs simulators that are both photorealistic and geometrically grounded at metric scale. The authors observe that vision-only reconstruction stays meter-level inaccurate and that this degrades NVS, RL training and evaluation reliability.
key_idea: Capture indoor-outdoor urban scenes with a handheld LiDAR-inertial-visual-GNSS scanner, use LIV-SLAM metric poses and point clouds to initialize and regularize 3DGS and to extract a collision mesh, and merge both into Isaac Sim USD scenes.
insight: Geometry source matters: the best vision-only reconstructor still has ~0.30 m / 5° error after scale alignment and meter-level raw error, and simulators built on such geometry make RL post-training degrade (Vid2Sim env) and evaluation success rates look much lower than in the grounded env. The appendix ablation shows that LiDAR poses/points only help NVS when used with a depth loss (PSNR 15.54 without vs 20.95 with), and that Difix3D+ view augmentation improves extrapolated views (PSNR 16.97→17.92) at a slight cost on interpolated views. Freezing Gaussian centers is worse on extrapolated views (17.10 vs 17.92).
method: Multi-sensor capture: SkylandX MetaCam Air (Livox Mid-360 LiDAR+IMU, RTK-GNSS, two 4K fisheye cameras); distance/rotation-triggered RGB capture, closed-loop dense training trajectories plus separate extrapolation trajectories, 5,000–10,000 m² scenes, ~1 FPS

LIV-SLAM reconstruction: proprietary MetaCam Studio fuses LiDAR-inertial-visual-GNSS into a globally consistent metric colorized point cloud and camera poses; masking of faces/plates (EgoBlur) and dynamic objects (YOLOv11); fisheye cropped to 120° pinhole

3DGS training: gsplat, Gaussians initialized from ~5M downsampled LiDAR points with KNN scale and density-inverse opacity; photometric + depth loss with depth rendered from initialized Gaussians as GT (means not frozen); 15k steps at 800×800
Training view augmentation: Difix3D+ self-training refines rendered novel views at sampled extrapolated poses, added with lower loss weight, with sampling radius growing over training (curriculum)

Collision mesh: voxelize point cloud into occupancy grid, marching cubes, crop by distance to trajectory, drop fragments <50 faces; combine mesh (physics) + 3DGS (renderer) in one USD scene for Isaac Sim

Task generation: Unity NavMesh baking and pathfinding for expert trajectories (point/image goal); replayed egocentric video fed to Gemini 2.5 Flash with two-stage JSON→instruction prompting plus manual spot checks for VLN
Benchmarks: camera-pose estimation (vision-only models vs LIV-SLAM GT), NVS, PPO RL post-training with distance-shaped reward, and pretrained navigation policy benchmark

setting.backbone: Benchmarked policies: NoMaD, CityWalker, MBRA (RL fine-tuned with PPO), NaVid, NaVILA (pretrained, evaluated only); 3DGS per scene optimized
setting.training_data: Wanderland dataset: 530 scenes, 420K frames, >100 h, 3.8M m² in NYC/Jersey City; RL uses the train split with sampled NavMesh start/goal pairs; Difix3D+ pretrained model for augmentation; Gemini 2.5 Flash for instructions
setting.observation: Rendered egocentric RGB from 3DGS (120° pinhole), goal specification as point/image/language
setting.action_space: Each policy's original action space (waypoint/velocity-type outputs), episodes capped at 1000 steps
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (3DGS + collision mesh in USD); Unity for NavMesh path generation
setting.privileged: none (GT LIV-SLAM poses/LiDAR used for building the environments and as ground truth for reconstruction evaluation, not by policies)

numbers_note: Paper's contribution is a dataset/simulator; no standard nav benchmark results. Numbers listed are Wanderland-native benchmark values (other baselines omitted). The evaluation-reliability figure (Vid2Sim vs Ours env bars) is only in a figure. The navigation benchmark table has all five policies; only the best (NaVILA) is listed here.
results: Wanderland's LIV-SLAM-based 3DGS gives the best interpolated NVS (PSNR 20.37, LPIPS 0.327 vs 3DGS/COLMAP 18.27/0.510) and the best extrapolated PSNR (17.92 vs 17.00 for 3DGUT). RL post-training in Wanderland improves all three policies (e.g. CityWalker SR +14%), whereas Vid2Sim envs degrade NoMaD/CityWalker. Best pretrained policy NaVILA reaches SR 0.47 indoor / 0.31 outdoor, so none exceeds 50%.
limitations: Capture at ~1 FPS gives sparse views, limiting rendering quality in complex scenes
Static scenes only; no pedestrians, vehicles or traffic dynamics
Reconstruction relies on proprietary MetaCam Studio LIV-SLAM and specialized hardware; VLN instructions are auto-generated by Gemini with only spot-check verification
